title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages): Grothendieck is building a purely order-theoretic 'analysis situs', a combinatorial model for tame or stratified topology.

- There is a lattice 𝓕 of 'figures'.
- Inside it sits a set M of 'lieux' (places). These behave like join-irreducible, in fact join-prime, elements.
- For F ∈ 𝓕, F̃ = {X ∈ M : X ≤ F}, and F = sup F̃.
- On M there is a 'shadow' relation ≪. For X ∈ M, Omb(X) = {Y ∈ M : Y ≪ X}; it is a closure-like set, roughly the closure or star of a stratum.
- Multomb(F) = {Omb(X) : X ∈ F̃} ⊂ P'(M), ordered by inclusion. This is a new 'figure' (a multi-figure) whose underlying set is |Multomb F| = Omb(F) = ∪_{X∈F̃} Omb(X).
- The previous page proves F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃ ⇔ Multomb(F) ⊂ Multomb(G) ⇔ Multomb(F) ≤ Multomb(G). The proof uses injectivity of X ↦ Omb(X).

This page:

(1) It finishes the proof of Corollary 1. For 'compatible' F, G one has (F∨G)~ = F̃ ∪ G̃, with F̃ and G̃ closed in it. Hence Multomb(F∨G) = Multomb(F) ∪ Multomb(G), with both pieces closed. This gives compatibility of the multi-figures and the first relation (**). The second relation, Multomb(F∧G) = Multomb(F) ∩ Multomb(G), follows from (F∧G)~ = F̃ ∩ G̃.

(2) NB: the converse fails. Take F and G reduced to two distinct lieux x, y. Then Multomb = {{x}} and {{y}}, which are compatible and disjoint, but x and y need not be. Grothendieck guesses the converse holds under some regularity hypothesis on 𝓕, with the marginal note 'vérifier plus tard'.

(3) Corollary 2: if F and G are disjoint, so are Multomb(F) and Multomb(G). This is formal from Cor. 1 together with (1.40) Multomb(∅_𝓕) = ∅, the least element of 𝓤.

(4) Statement of a Proposition: F ≪ G ⇔ Multomb(F) ≪ Multomb(G). The proof on the next page uses the canonical retraction φ_F : Omb(F) → F̃, which sends Y to the smallest X ∈ F̃ with Y ≪ X.

Purpose: show that F ↦ Multomb(F) embeds the lattice of figures, with its shadow relation, into a lattice of multi-figures. It preserves order, compatible joins, meets, the empty figure, disjointness and ≪. This is a step toward a self-contained combinatorial category of 'figures' modelling tame spaces.
errors: (F∨G)~ = F̃ ∪ G̃ silently requires lieux to be join-prime (e.g. join-irreducibles in a distributive lattice); it is not stated on this page, though presumably assumed earlier.
The regularity hypothesis under which the converse of the NB 'would be true' is left unspecified and unchecked ('vérifier plus tard'). It is a gap, not an error.
Minor: the proof of Cor. 1 only gestures at why compatibility of the multi-figures follows ('donc ... et la première relation'); this is clear enough given the definitions.

ideas.what: Multomb functor/map sending a figure to the family of shadows of its constituent lieux, compatible with ∨ (under compatibility), ∧, ∅, disjointness
ideas.modern_name: order-embedding of a distributive lattice into a lattice of down-sets (Birkhoff-type representation) with closure ('star/closure of strata') data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (representation of distributive lattices); Alexandrov (poset topologies)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Analysis situs notes (1986); the general tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism

ideas.what: Counterexample showing compatibility/disjointness of multi-shadows does not reflect back to figures (two distinct lieux)
ideas.modern_name: failure of reflection of a relation under an order embedding

ideas.what: Canonical retraction Omb(F) → F̃ (smallest lieu of F shadowing a given Y), used to characterize F ≪ G
ideas.modern_name: closure/retraction onto a sub-poset; nearest-stratum map in a stratified poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that the converse (compatibility of Multomb(F), Multomb(G) implies compatibility of F, G) holds under an unspecified regularity hypothesis, and flags it to check later.
missed.quote: Mais il serait vrai sous quelque[?] hypothèse de régularité ... vérifier plus tard
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It belongs to the broader unrealized 1986 programme of a combinatorial 'analysis situs' for tame or stratified spaces, which relates to o-minimal and stratified-space foundations. In itself this is a small order-theoretic question.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lattice and order-theoretic lemmas inside an unpublished framework. The framework itself (figures, lieux, ombres) is little known, but this page contains no striking result.
transcription_corrections: The page number at top reads 24 (consistent with page 24 of 93), not 29.
NB: 'même si F et G sont réduits à deux lieux distincts x et y', not 'réduits [?] — en lieux distincts'.
NB: the multi-shadows 'sont compatibles et disjoints', not 'compatibles et non disjoints'.
Second relation: '(F∧G)~ = F̃ ∩ G̃'; the transcription's \widetilde{F∩G} is a ∧/∩ ambiguity.
The margin note 'vérifier plus tard' sits beside the NB's last line.
(1.40): the parenthetical is likely '(plus petit élément de 𝓤)' or similar; it is uncertain.
